Who We Are:

Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.

The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.

What We Value:

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

  • Seek Excellence.
  • Be Selective To Be Effective.
  • Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
  • Disagree Transparently.
  • Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
  • Build Dream Teams.

Who You Are

You are a commissioning leader who has taken large-scale, mission-critical data center facilities from equipment acceptance through energization, functional performance testing, and integrated systems testing, and who has done it across multiple facilities at once. You understand the electrical, mechanical, and controls systems well enough to challenge a test script, read a trend log, and know when a result does not prove design intent. You understand the commissioning process well enough to adapt it, not just follow it, and you can rebuild the test sequence when conditions change. That includes authoring the MOPs and risk controls for completing IST and load-based validation after early turnover, in live or partially occupied environments, without lowering the performance requirements the original plan was designed to prove. You lead teams from the front, hold contractors, OEMs, and third parties to a high standard, and refuse to let schedule pressure compromise a readiness gate. You are equally comfortable on the data hall floor with a startup technician and in the conference room briefing senior leadership on readiness, risk, and forecast. You believe the digital economy depends on infrastructure that is proven before it is energized for customers, and you take ownership of making that proof rigorous.

What You'll Do

As Senior Manager, Commissioning at Galaxy's Helios campus in Afton, TX, you will lead all commissioning efforts across the campus on behalf of Galaxy as owner and developer. You will report to the VP, Campus Construction Manager and manage a team of three Commissioning Managers, each assigned to a data center facility. You will work closely with the general contractor's on-site team and Galaxy's third-party commissioning agent, and you will partner with Construction, Pre-Construction, Design Engineering, and Operations to ensure every facility is installed, tested, and proven to design intent, and handed to operations ready for customer service. You will set the commissioning standard for the campus and hold every facility to it.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own Campus Commissioning: Serve as Galaxy's single point of accountability for commissioning across the Helios campus, from design intent review through Level 1-5 commissioning, integrated systems testing (IST), and turnover to operations. Set the campus-wide standards and quality bar.
  • Lead the Commissioning Team: Manage three Commissioning Managers, each embedded at a data center facility. Standardize methods and reporting, balance resources across facilities, and develop talent.
  • Define and Enforce the Commissioning Plan: Own the campus commissioning plan and its alignment to the Owner's Project Requirements and Basis of Design, including acceptance criteria, test standards, and readiness gates. Ensure these are written into GC, trade, and OEM scopes.
  • Validate Testing and Design Intent: Review and approve test scripts, sequences of operation, and IST scenarios across critical power, mechanical cooling, and BAS/EPMS controls and telemetry. Ensure testing proves design intent, redundancy, and failure-mode response.
  • Drive Execution with the General Contractor: Integrate commissioning into the Primavera P6 master schedule and work daily with the GC's commissioning lead and trade partners to confirm readiness, resourcing, and OEM startup support. Hold the GC accountable through readiness reviews, deficiency tracking, and commercial remedies.
  • Direct the Third-Party Commissioning Agent and Issue Closeout: Manage the scope and performance of Galaxy's third-party agent, challenge findings, and maintain a campus-level issues log. Drive every item through root cause, corrective action, and retest to closure.
  • Coordinate Energization and OFCI Equipment: Plan utility energization and load bank testing, enforcing safe work during energized testing in partnership with EHS. Align OFCI equipment delivery, factory testing, and manufacturer startup with the commissioning sequence. Adapt the commissioning sequence and author MOPs to complete Level 4-5 and IST activities after early data hall turnover, without lowering acceptance criteria.
  • Deliver Operational Readiness and Customer Acceptance: Partner with Galaxy Operations and customer delivery teams on documentation, training, operating procedures, witnessed testing, and formal turnover, ensuring each facility meets acceptance criteria at handoff.
  • Report Readiness and Standardize: Provide candid readiness reporting to the VP and senior leadership, and feed lessons learned into design standards, specifications, and Pre-Construction planning.
  • Validate Controls, BAS/EPMS, and Telemetry: Ensure the BAS, EPMS, and associated controls are commissioned as a system, not just as individual points lists. Verify point-to-point integrity, alarm and trend configuration, and operator visibility across all critical power and mechanical systems, including through failure scenarios such as loss of utility, loss of a controls network or server, communication failure, and transfer events. Confirm that telemetry remains accurate and actionable so Operations can see, diagnose, and respond to any failure while redundancy is maintained.

What We're Looking For:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of experience commissioning mission-critical facilities, including 5+ years on large-scale data centers, with at least 3 years in a leadership role directing commissioning through Level 5 / IST.
  • Demonstrated success leading commissioning across multiple concurrent facilities on a single campus.
  • Experience managing and developing commissioning managers or engineers.
  • Deep technical knowledge of critical power systems, including medium- and low-voltage distribution, protective relaying, UPS, batteries, generators, and transfer systems.
  • Deep technical knowledge of mechanical cooling systems, including chilled water plants, heat rejection, air handling, pumps, and associated controls.
  • Working knowledge of BMS, EPMS, and SCADA architectures, sequences of operation, and fire and life safety system integration.
  • Experience developing, executing, and witnessing IST, including failure-mode and fault scenarios.
  • Familiarity with ASHRAE Guideline 0, NETA acceptance testing standards, NFPA 70E, and NFPA 110.
  • Experience directing GC commissioning teams and third-party commissioning agents, with strong command of test documentation, issue tracking, and P6 schedule integration.
  • Familiarity with Procore, Primavera P6, Bluebeam, SharePoint, and commissioning management platforms.
  • Full-time, on-site presence at Helios (Afton, TX)
  • Preferred: Professional Engineer (PE) license or commissioning certification (e.g., CxA, CCP, BCxP), prior owner-side or owner's representative experience, and OSHA 30.

What You Bring:

  • A track record of leading and developing high-performing technical teams.
  • The conviction to hold readiness gates under schedule pressure, backed by data and clear communication.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to influence technical and executive stakeholders.
  • Sound judgment under pressure and a bias toward early, honest escalation.
  • A commitment to safety, rigor, and executional excellence.
  • A passion for building world-class infrastructure that supports the growth of the digital economy.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus
  • Paid Time Off
  • Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents
  • Company Paid Holidays (14)
  • 3% 401(k) company contribution
  • Generous paid Parental Leave
  • Free virtual coaching and counseling sessions through Headspace
  • Opportunities to learn about the Crypto industry
  • Free daily snacks and daily meals
  • Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues
  • Employee Resource Groups

*Benefits may vary depending on location.

Apply now and join us on our mission to engineer a new economic paradigm.

 

Galaxy respects diversity and seeks to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and job applicants for employment without regard to actual or perceived age, race, color, creed, religion, sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), gender identity or gender expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital or partnership or caregiver status, ancestry, national origin, citizenship status, disability, military or veteran status, protected medical condition as defined by applicable state or local law, genetic information or predisposing genetic characteristic, or other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Kamino

Kamino's mission is to create liquidity and utility for every asset. We want the world's best investments to be available through the financial platforms people already trust, and we want investors to be able to borrow against what they own when they need liquidity, instead of having to sell.

Today, the most valuable assets in the world are often the least useful to own. Trillions of dollars sit in private markets, behind high minimums and holding periods that can run for years. Tokenization is starting to move these assets onto shared, programmable infrastructure, but putting an asset onchain is only the first step. To be useful, it still needs distribution, compliance, servicing, credit and liquidity.

Kamino already runs the credit and liquidity engine at scale. It is the largest credit protocol on Solana and the largest credit platform for real-world assets onchain, with more than $650 billion in cumulative transaction volume and more than $20 billion in loans originated.

Now we are building the rest of that system for institutions. Kamino recently named Yieldstreet co-founder Michael Weisz as CEO and is building a new HQ in New York, alongside the asset managers and financial platforms that will shape this market. Almost none of that market exists yet, and we intend to build it.

Legal & Compliance | New York, NY | Full-time | Four days in office | Reports to the CEO

The opportunity

Kamino is hiring its first General Counsel to lead legal and compliance globally, build the U.S. operating foundation, and hire the legal and compliance team over the next 6–12 months.

Kamino is expanding in the United States and building a team in New York to lead this next phase. We are looking for a General Counsel who will own Kamino's global legal and compliance function and turn that ambition into an executable operating model.

As General Counsel, you will be accountable for legal and compliance matters across the globe. Your immediate focus will be establishing Kamino's U.S. operating foundation, while setting the global legal strategy and overseeing regulatory matters outside the U.S.

This is a build-with-product role, not a pure sign-off function. Working directly with the CEO and leaders across product, engineering, business development and operations, you will shape institutional products and partnerships from inception and turn regulatory sophistication into a commercial advantage. Within your first 6–12 months, you will begin building the legal and compliance team that will scale with Kamino.

What you'll do

Global legal and compliance leadership

  • Serve as Kamino's chief legal officer and principal legal adviser to the CEO, leadership team and the Foundation.

  • Own the global legal and compliance function across all Kamino entities and jurisdictions, including corporate, commercial, regulatory, intellectual property, employment, privacy and disputes.

  • Set Kamino's global regulatory strategy, coordinating U.S. work with frameworks such as MiCA and with other key markets.

  • Establish and oversee Kamino's global compliance program, including AML, sanctions, risk assessment, policies and monitoring.

  • Manage legal risk, disputes and any regulatory inquiries or investigations worldwide.

  • Own the legal and compliance budget, and select and manage external counsel and regulatory advisers across jurisdictions.

Building the legal and compliance team

  • Design the target structure of Kamino's legal and compliance organization, aligned to the company's product, geographic and institutional roadmap.

  • Begin hiring within the first 6–12 months, prioritizing the roles Kamino needs most (for example, compliance, product and regulatory counsel, and commercial counsel).

  • Recruit, develop and lead a high-performing team, and set the standards, tools and ways of working the function operates by.

  • Decide what to build in-house and what to keep with external counsel as Kamino scales.

U.S. legal architecture and governance

  • Design Kamino's U.S. legal and regulatory operating model, including entity roles, legal posture and the approval process for new products.

  • Partner with executive leadership to develop and refine the U.S. roadmap in line with Kamino's overall strategy, with legal and regulatory considerations built into planning from the outset.

  • Advise where Kamino should operate as infrastructure, where third parties must assume regulated or managerial responsibilities, and what Kamino should deliberately avoid.

Product roadmap and institutional strategy

  • Embed with product and engineering on lending markets, vaults, leverage products, points and rewards programs, token launches, tokenized real-world assets and other new capabilities.

  • Translate regulatory risk into concrete product design choices before products are built, rather than layering legal review on after decisions have been made.

  • Create repeatable legal and diligence processes for onboarding asset managers, curators, distribution platforms and supporting service providers.

  • Lead or support negotiations involving integrations, institutional pilots, data, technology, custody, servicing, tokenization, credit and liquidity.

Securities, commodities and regulatory analysis

  • Apply the Howey and Reves tests, related case law and CFTC jurisdictional principles to evaluate whether tokens, yield products or trading features could be characterized as securities or commodity derivatives under U.S. law.

  • Track and interpret federal legislation, SEC and CFTC rulemaking and guidance, state frameworks, and executive or agency policy affecting DeFi, staking, stablecoins, custody and tokenized assets, alongside major developments in other jurisdictions.

  • Assess money-transmitter licensing, BitLicense-style regimes and other state-level requirements for Kamino's operating entities, and equivalent licensing requirements in other markets.

Regulatory engagement, compliance and policy

  • Represent Kamino in proactive and responsive interactions with the SEC, CFTC, FinCEN, OFAC, relevant state regulators and, where relevant, non-U.S. regulators.

  • Advise on Bank Secrecy Act obligations, FinCEN guidance, OFAC sanctions screening and Travel Rule implications for non-custodial infrastructure and any centralized touchpoints.

  • Contribute to industry advocacy and help shape Kamino's comments on proposed rules through appropriate trade associations and policy organizations.

  • Build regulatory literacy across product, engineering and go-to-market teams so that sound judgment is applied without legal reviewing every routine decision.

  • Maintain legal memoranda, risk assessments, policies and decision logs for product launches.

What success looks like

Building the global legal and compliance foundation

Within the first six months

  • Make Kamino operational in the United States for its approved initial scope within 90 days, including the ability to employ its team, maintain its New York presence, enter contracts and advance approved business development and pilot activity.

  • Establish clear boundaries, decision rights and escalation processes.

  • Complete the licensing and registration analysis for Kamino's planned U.S. activities and establish the roadmap for any required approvals.

  • Map Kamino's legal and compliance obligations in its other key jurisdictions and put oversight and external counsel coverage in place.

  • Put the initial compliance, contracting, governance and documentation framework in place.

  • Produce executable legal pathways for Kamino's highest-priority institutional pilots and partnerships.

  • Agree a legal and compliance team plan and hiring priorities with the CEO, and begin recruiting for the first roles.

By the end of the first year

  • Make the first legal and compliance hires and have the core team operating.

  • Expand the initial U.S. structure into a scalable operating model capable of supporting institutional products and partnerships.

  • Establish repeatable legal processes for asset-manager onboarding, distribution integrations and institutional product launches.

  • Enable Kamino's priority institutional pilots to proceed with clear approvals, responsibilities and risk boundaries.

  • Implement practical global governance and compliance systems that protect Kamino without slowing product development.

  • Build a trusted network of external counsel, regulatory advisers and industry relationships across Kamino's key jurisdictions.

  • Set the longer-term roadmap for Kamino's global legal and compliance organization.

Why this role matters

The infrastructure decisions being made today will shape how institutions participate in onchain markets for years. Kamino has already built a proven credit and liquidity engine. The next challenge is to create the legal and operating framework, starting in the U.S., that allows that technology to serve asset managers, distribution platforms and financial institutions at scale.

As Kamino's first General Counsel, you will sit at the intersection of law, product and company building. You will help determine what Kamino builds, how it operates and which institutional opportunities it can pursue, and you will build the team that carries that work forward.

Who we are looking for

A practical legal builder and leader

Required

  • J.D. and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

  • Twelve or more years of relevant legal and regulatory experience, including meaningful time in-house at a digital-asset or fintech company, in a law-firm digital-assets practice, or at a relevant regulator.

  • Experience leading a legal or compliance function, or a significant part of one, as the senior legal adviser to executive leadership.

  • A track record of hiring, managing and developing lawyers and compliance professionals.

  • Direct, hands-on experience with DeFi protocols and digital-asset market structure, including lending markets, automated market makers, liquidity vaults, staking and onchain governance.

  • Demonstrated experience interacting with the SEC, CFTC or other financial regulators through inquiries, comment letters, roundtables, no-action processes or enforcement matters.

  • Strong working knowledge of U.S. securities and commodities laws, the Bank Secrecy Act, sanctions requirements and relevant state regulatory frameworks as applied to digital assets.

  • Working knowledge of cross-border digital-asset regulatory frameworks, including MiCA and the U.K. FCA regime, and experience managing legal matters across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Fluency in the current U.S. legislative and regulatory landscape, with the ability to convert fast-moving developments into practical guidance.

  • Sound judgment and comfort operating where the law is still developing, with the confidence to recommend a course of action rather than simply identify risk.

  • Excellent communication with engineers, product leaders, commercial teams and boards in a way that supports product velocity.

  • Thoughtful use of modern technology, including AI, to improve legal research, drafting, regulatory tracking and execution.

Forward Deployed Product Manager

Location: U.S. (Remote, but must be based in the United States) Travel: Depending on the assigned engagement, substantial travel to state government partner sites may be expected Clearance: Must be eligible and able to pass a government background check

 
 

ABOUT SPRUCE

Spruce builds privacy-preserving, standards-based digital identity and credentialing solutions that give individuals control of their information while enabling governments and enterprises to deliver secure, interoperable services. We partner with private and public-sector organizations to modernize how identity is issued, verified, and used.

THE ROLE

We are seeking a Forward Deployed Product Manager to sit alongside our government customers during discovery, architecture, and design - sometimes while engineering is building - and help them work out what they actually need, and why.

You will support specific deployments, beginning with a statewide education and workforce credential initiative. Much of this work is customer-driven today and requires hands-on engagement with individual implementations, even as we work toward consolidating these efforts into reusable Spruce products. Holding both of those at once is the job. Beyond product discovery, you also own ecosystem adoption - getting issuers to issue, verifiers to verify, and learners to adopt - with startup-style resourcefulness and measurable KPIs.

The surface area is broad. One week you may be shaping the roadmap for a statewide digital identity wallet, the next a citizen-facing portal, the next the APIs and microservices underneath. You are responsible for the end-to-end product picture and for understanding how those pieces fit together.

This is not a roadmap-and-quarterly-planning role. We move quickly, put work in front of small pilot groups, and let evidence change the plan. At the same time, this is identity infrastructure, where security, accessibility, and reliability genuinely matter. Knowing what can be iterated on quickly and what absolutely cannot is central to doing this job well. In some cases, you may source and build that pilot group yourself.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

1. CUSTOMER-EMBEDDED DISCOVERY

  • Work directly with state government partners through discovery, architecture, and design

  • Understand their users, policy environment, constraints, and workflows first-hand

  • Look past stated requirements to the underlying problem the customer is actually trying to solve

  • Act as a trusted product advisor to public sector stakeholders

2. END-TO-END PRODUCT OWNERSHIP

  • Hold the full product picture across a statewide wallet, citizen-facing portals, and the APIs and services beneath them

  • Help partners shape their roadmap and priorities, and make sure what gets built solves the real problem

  • Partner closely with engineering, design, and delivery leads from definition through deployment

3. HANDS-ON USER RESEARCH

  • Personally design and run research: talk to users, stakeholders, and end users directly, conduct discovery, prototype where appropriate

  • Synthesize what you learn and translate it into product decisions and roadmap direction

  • Bring user evidence into conversations where requirements are often treated as fixed

There is no research team sitting behind this role. You do this work yourself.

4. INFLUENCE IN A PUBLIC SECTOR CONTEXT

  • Navigate government relationships thoughtfully while introducing evidence that may challenge stated priorities

  • Influence direction without damaging the relationship

  • Communicate clearly across users, policy, technical constraints, and business priorities

5. PATTERN RECOGNITION AND PRODUCT STRATEGY

  • Identify patterns across customers and ask what individual deployments teach us about broader product opportunities

  • Connect customer needs to reusable product capabilities

  • Recognize where a problem extends beyond a single agency, and shape product strategy from evidence rather than incoming requests

6. JUDGMENT ABOUT PACE VERSUS RISK

  • Put work in front of small pilot groups early and let findings redirect the roadmap

  • Draw clear lines around what cannot be iterated on loosely: security, accessibility, and reliability

  • Make and defend those calls with engineering and with customers

7. ECOSYSTEM BUILDING & ADOPTION

  • Drive adoption of digital credentials across the ecosystem - onboard issuers, verifiers, and institutional partners with startup GTM resourcefulness

  • Find high-leverage partnerships (university research programs, workforce boards, employer networks) that multiply impact beyond your own direct effort

  • Own adoption KPIs and find creative, resourceful ways to move them

  • Act as a credible product advisor to executive stakeholders including agency directors, university leadership, and ecosystem partners

WHAT YOU BRING

  • 6–10+ years of product experience at startups or building new product initiatives

  • Time in an early-stage environment where you personally shipped product and moved quickly

  • Zero-to-one experience: you have taken a product from nothing to shipped, or identified and pursued entirely new opportunities

  • Ideally, meaningful experience in education, workforce development, or adjacent sectors

  • Experience in government or another highly regulated environment

  • Genuine customer-embedded experience - forward-deployed product, solutions PM, implementation, or founder-led delivery all count

  • Demonstrated, hands-on user research: you have designed and run discovery yourself and turned it into product decisions

  • Enough technical depth to sit comfortably with engineers and hold your own on APIs, services, and system design. You do not need to be an engineer

  • Comfort with ambiguity, a broad surface area, and shifting priorities

  • Credible at the executive level - comfortable holding a room with agency directors, university chancellors, and institutional partners

  • Based in the U.S. and excited to engage directly with state government partners

  • Passion for workforce development and expanding opportunity through technology

NICE TO HAVE

  • Background in digital identity, IAM / ICAM, credentialing, or authentication systems

  • Familiarity with accessibility standards, FedRAMP, or NIST frameworks

  • Experience navigating public sector procurement and contracting environments

  • Prior engineering or deeply technical systems experience

  • Experience building or growing multi-sided ecosystems, marketplaces, or platform adoption

  • Background in education technology, learning and employment records, or workforce development programs

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

  • Shape identity systems that millions of residents will actually use

  • Work directly with senior government stakeholders on mission-critical infrastructure

  • Operate at the intersection of policy, engineering, research, and real-world delivery

  • Help turn individual state deployments into durable product capability

  • Help build the education and workforce credential ecosystem that connects citizens to opportunity

  • Join a small, high-trust team where autonomy and judgment matter

About Mesh

At Mesh, our mission is to enable consumers to pay and be paid with any asset. Today, trillions of dollars in tokenized assets exist but remain largely unusable for everyday commerce. Mesh is bridging this gap by making crypto payments reliable, useful, and ubiquitous. We combine a powerful orchestration engine with a seamless consumer app to unlock liquidity for the world. Overview

You will build the systems that connect Mesh's products to its books, and produce the revenue metrics that run the business. Working with Sales, Product and Engineering, you design and ship the integrations, billing logic and reconciliation tools behind our deposit, on/off-ramp, OTC and card products. You own revenue operations end to end: Salesforce, revenue reporting and commission administration. This is a builder role: most of your time goes into shipping systems, not running reports by hand.

  • Own the finance and revenue systems architecture and integrations across Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, Bill.com, card programs and the data warehouse.
  • Co-build with Product and Engineering the billing engine for ramps and payments: partner fee schedules, markups, revenue splits and monthly partner settlements.

Compliance is where Elliptic began and where our commercial core sits today. Some of the world's largest exchanges, banks and government agencies rely on our screening, monitoring and investigation products, and the industry they serve is at an inflection point. Compliance teams everywhere are looking to AI to make their work dramatically more efficient, freeing their people to focus on the judgement calls that genuinely need a human, with every automated decision auditable and explainable. Elliptic is building that future with our customers, not just for them, and this role owns it.

You will lead the product managers responsible for our core compliance portfolio, spanning wallet and transaction screening, continuous monitoring, on-chain investigations and risk configuration, and you will drive the product side of our agentic compliance programme alongside our design partners. Much of what you build will have no precedent. You will be inventing the category, inside the company with the data, intelligence and customer trust to win it.

This is a player-coach role reporting to the VP of Product. You will lead and grow a team of product managers and personally own some of the hardest problems on the roadmap. The product organisation is centred in London with a growing US presence.

 
 

What you'll do

  • Own the vision, strategy and roadmap for Elliptic's compliance portfolio, and define what these products become as AI reshapes how compliance work gets done.

  • Lead product for our agentic compliance programme: AI capabilities that make compliance work faster and better, with auditability and explainability designed in from the start.

  • Lead, coach and grow a team of product managers. Hire well, develop people deliberately, and set the standard for how a modern, AI-augmented PM works. Developing product talent is a core output of this role, not a side effect.

  • Stay obsessively close to customers, in creative ways: Methods such as design partnerships, analyst shadowing, product instrumentation, and internal dogfooding before anything ships come naturally to you to increase the chances of success. Convert ambiguous market signal into a clear view of what to build and why.

  • Prioritise ruthlessly. Demand will always exceed capacity. Sequence zero-to-one bets against the needs of products customers depend on today, and say yes or no credibly, with reasoning people can engage with.

  • Execute with rigour, raising velocity and quality together. Own outcomes, not shipping dates. Use AI across your own workflow and your team's to learn faster and ship better at the same time, in a domain where mistakes carry real consequences.

 
 

What this role is not

  • Not a compliance officer role. You are building the products compliance teams use, not running a compliance programme.

  • Not a caretaker role. The core products are successful and deeply embedded; the mandate is reinvention.

  • Not a management-only layer. You will lead product managers and personally do product work on the hardest problems.

 
 

Who we're looking for

  • 10+ years building software products, including leading and developing product managers, with people who are better because they worked with you.

  • A genuine zero-to-one track record: an ambiguous problem in a complex domain, taken from nothing to a product real users depend on.

  • Depth in financial crime compliance from the product side (transaction monitoring, screening, KYC/EDD or investigations), built inside an exchange, a bank, a fintech or a compliance technology company.

  • Working knowledge of crypto and blockchain as a baseline; deep blockchain analytics experience is a strong plus.

  • AI-native: AI is embedded in how you work and build every day, you have shipped AI or agentic capabilities to production, and you raise the AI capability of teams around you. If AI has not materially changed how you build product in the last two years, this is not the right role.

  • Deep executional rigour: you break complex problems into shippable steps, sweat the details that determine quality, and reliably carry work over the line.

  • High self-sufficiency: you find high-value opportunities no one assigned you, create clarity rather than wait for it, and are comfortable owning a broad remit while the map is still being drawn.

  • Continuous systems thinking: you look for the repeatable system behind every one-off fix, building leverage so each problem solved makes the whole team permanently faster.

  • Restlessness about velocity and quality: you treat "that's just how long it takes" as a claim to be tested.

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

As a Global Investigator on the triage team, you are the first line of operational response in a fast-moving crypto disruption pipeline. You process inbound victim complaints, validate the output of our AI investigation tooling, and route cases into the investigative workflows that lead to frozen scam proceeds, takedowns, and recovered assets. You hold the disposition pen: your call is what turns a complaint into a freeze, an escalation, a recovery handoff, a victim notification, or a close.

The impact you will have:

  • Validate and route hundreds of complaint dispositions each week, feeding a live asset-recovery pipeline that gets stolen funds frozen before they move.

  • Use AI first-pass output as a co-pilot and catch the errors that matter, such as false positives, merged syndicates, and misclassified scam patterns, before they propagate downstream.

  • Enrich complaint selectors with a broad stack of commercial data-source integrations and on-chain and off-chain checks to decide what is actionable.

  • Own clean shift handoffs so the around-the-clock operation never drops a lead, keeping the US-hours queue moving for the rest of the triage team.

  • Feed structured signal back to engineering on where the AI triage model misses, so it gets more precise every week.

What we’re looking for:

  • Investigative or analytical experience in the private or public sector. 1-3 years is fine; we want people who want to grow into deep crypto expertise.

  • Strong AI fluency, meaning comfort using AI tools as a daily co-pilot to work a high-volume queue, with the judgment to know when the output is wrong.

  • Baseline crypto knowledge and the ability to recognize threat types such as investment scams, pig-butchering, and ransomware, and comfort pairing that with AI-assisted analysis.

  • Able to prioritize and work independently, with clear written handoffs, during hours when the rest of the team is offline.

  • Receptive to feedback from experienced tracers and engineers, and motivated to improve the triage process rather than only clear tickets.

  • US Citizenship required

  • Ability to obtain Public Trust clearance

About the Team:

  • The team pairs seasoned crypto tracers with rising investigators. Triage investigators sit alongside experienced Global Investigators and intelligence-trained individual contributors, and the seat is built to accelerate your development toward deeper tracing work.

  • The work is operationally hard: high volume, real victims, and time-sensitive calls where a fast, accurate disposition can be the difference between funds frozen and funds gone.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • Primary coverage during US business hours in your local time zone, holding triage throughput while colleagues in other regions are offline.

  • Distributed, not distant: async-first handoffs, clear written updates, and tight coordination with global teammates on time-sensitive items.

Required online and collaboration hours:

  • Schedule: Standard North American EST business hours preferred, with overlap for daily handover to and from other regions.

On-Call Responsibilities:

  • Schedule: Formal on-call rotation for high-priority events, such as active hacks, law-enforcement support, and other time-sensitive matters.

  • Frequency: Weekly rotation, with occasional weekend coverage; remote standby (free to go about your day and respond when paged), not worksite-bound.

Travel Requirements:

  • Schedule: Minimal; occasional team or mission offsites.

Onsite Requirements:

  • Distributed/remote role with no routine onsite requirement.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within your first 30 days, you are clearing live complaint surges end to end, turning raw victim reports into actionable freezes and escalations the same day they arrive.

  • Within 90 days, your prioritization calls are routinely accepted by Global Investigators, measurably shortening the time between a report landing and funds being frozen.

  • Each week, your feedback to engineering sharpens the AI triage model, so the whole team catches more recoverable cases with less manual review.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

Your Role

Every serious AI team evaluating infrastructure asks the same question: will this actually run my workload better, faster, or cheaper than what I have today? Most vendors answer with slides. We want to answer with benchmarks on the customer's own workload, and then design the production architecture that delivers on them.

As our Founding Solutions Architect, your mission is to make Prime Intellect the technical winner in every deal. You will own the path from workload discovery through architecture, benchmark, proof of concept, and production design. You will sit with customers' ML engineers to understand what they are actually training and serving — GPU type, cluster requirements, networking, utilization and performance objectives — then design the right architecture on Prime infrastructure, run the POC against their baseline and the competitive alternatives, and turn latency, throughput, utilization, and cost results into a technical business case that holds up under scrutiny.

This is a founding role. There is no playbook yet for how we prove technical wins; you will write it. The benchmark methodologies, reference architectures, and POC frameworks you build will become how Prime Intellect sells to every lab and enterprise that follows.

Responsibilities

Technical Discovery & Architecture

  • Lead deep technical discovery across training, post-training, and inference workloads

  • Understand each customer's GPU requirements, cluster topology, networking, storage, utilization patterns, and performance objectives

  • Design customer architectures on Prime infrastructure that meet those objectives and are ready for production

  • Partner with engineering on migration and deployment requirements so what we design is what gets shipped

Benchmarks, POCs & the Technical Business Case

  • Own workload benchmarks and proofs of concept against customer baselines and competitive alternatives

  • Translate latency, throughput, utilization, and cost results into a defensible technical business case for ML engineers and executive buyers alike

  • Set the standard for benchmark quality: methodology, reproducibility, and honest comparison

  • Drive time to technical validation down with every deal

Playbooks & Platform Adoption

  • Develop repeatable benchmark and reference-architecture playbooks that scale beyond you

  • Support technical evaluation and adoption of Model Factory, bringing customers from compute onto the full training stack

  • Feed what you learn from customer workloads back into product and research priorities

What We're Looking For

  • Strong ML infrastructure, distributed systems, cloud, or GPU-compute background

  • Working knowledge of modern training and inference stacks, CUDA/GPU environments, and model-serving patterns

  • Customer-facing experience in solutions architecture, sales engineering, forward-deployed engineering, or a similar role

  • Ability to communicate fluently with both ML engineers and executive stakeholders — and to know which conversation you are in

  • A strong bias toward proving claims with real customer workloads and benchmarks rather than slides

  • High ownership — you see gaps and build the fix before anyone asks

  • AI-native in how you work: you use LLMs, automation, and programmatic tools to move faster

Bonus:

  • Hands-on experience running or optimizing large-scale distributed training (FSDP, Megatron, DeepSpeed, or similar) or high-throughput inference (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM)

  • Experience benchmarking across hardware generations (H100, H200, GB200) and interconnects (InfiniBand, RoCE)

  • Background at a GPU cloud, neocloud, hyperscaler AI team, or frontier lab infrastructure team

  • Experience building a solutions or forward-deployed function from scratch

How We Measure Success

Technical win rate · POC-to-commercial conversion · Time to technical validation · Benchmark quality · Deployment readiness · Model Factory technical attach

Why This Role

You will be the technical face of Prime Intellect in every deal that matters, working directly with the ML teams at labs and enterprises deciding where to build — and with our own research and engineering teams on what the platform needs to win. You will see more real-world training and inference workloads in a year than most engineers see in a career, and you will define how a new category of infrastructure proves itself.

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Our regional marketing efforts involve crafting and executing tailored marketing plans that resonate with local audiences, as well as spearheading our most significant conferences and sponsorships that drive go-to-market (GTM) success and business growth. Join us and be part of a culture that celebrates teamwork, innovates boldly, and makes a meaningful impact.

What you’ll do

You’ll be part of the EMEA Marketing team and be able to craft our enterprise and industry marketing strategy for the UK market while developing a strong trusted relationship working hand-in-hand with sales teams to drive successful user outcomes. The UK Enterprise Marketing Manager will define and execute field marketing program activations for integrated campaigns, targeted regional campaigns aligned to sales priorities, mid-funnel programs to accelerate leads and pipeline, high-tough programs, and Account Based Marketing. The ideal candidate is data-driven, and has an unbridled passion for working hand-in-hand with sales teams to drive successful user outcomes. As a key member of the EMEA Marketing team, this is a great opportunity to build and have an impact on the business.

Responsibilities

  • Craft enterprise marketing strategy and execute field marketing programs across enterprise customer segments (established enterprises, digital native businesses, software platforms), with emphasis on industry focused programs while solidly collaborating across key GTM stakeholders.
  • Own key business and revenue metrics across the sales funnel (pipeline) and customer growth and retention. 
  • Lead local Customer Marketing programs, ranging from case study creation to customer speaking engagements.
  • Partner with EMEA demand generation and product marketing to refine our targeting and segmentation, and to identify, scope, and produce or localize compelling content, marketing assets and programs to drive demand.
  • Define and execute full funnel UK marketing plans including digital marketing, demand generation campaigns, sales prospecting programs and ABM, executive engagement, virtual and in-person field events, and third party tradeshows and conferences as well as amplifying Stripe brand with users’ voices though case study production.
  • Track, measure, and communicate program results, continually optimize for efficiency and scale, and seek to generate new global best practices through experimental efforts. 
  • Be creative in finding new ways of advising a diverse range of enterprise personas about the value Stripe brings to businesses.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 7+ years of relevant B2B marketing experience in the UK Enterprise Technology market across multiple customer segments including specific experience with localizing global content, event management, field marketing, Account-based marketing and multi-touch campaigns to generate demand.
  • Proven track record of defining and executing B2B marketing strategies that deliver against funnel metrics and KPIs.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including being able to convey complex topics with simplicity.
  • Experience delivering tailored marketing content and experiences for customer segments spanning from early stage startups to the largest enterprise companies.
  • Superb organization and project management skills and the capacity to manage multiple complex projects at once.
  • Experience scaling through/and or leveraging agency and contractor resources.
  • Understanding and/or experience with CRM/Salesforce, account-based marketing, events marketing and email marketing tactics and technology

Preferred qualifications

  • A startup mentality with a bias to action and the ability to flex in a fast-paced industry and work environment.
  • Experience marketing B2B cloud services and/or software solutions.
  • Excellent analytical skills and the ability to craft actionable insights from complex data.
  • Resourceful, creative and dedicated to achieving operational and creative excellence.
  • Understanding of the payments, financial technology, and/or ecommerce industries and partner ecosystems.
  • Demonstrated success delivering marketing programs with and through consulting and technology partners.

Payments Product Sales is a team of deep functional and technical specialists who lead and advise on opportunities for some of the most strategically important products in Stripe’s portfolio. We work alongside Stripe’s Core Sales and Customer Success teams to help users adopt products that improve their payment experiences, support international growth, and create new sources of revenue.

We are hiring an Account Executive, Product - Buy Now Pay Later to grow adoption of Klarna and Affirm among Stripe users across APAC. Based in Australia, this role will have an initial emphasis on Australia and other priority APAC markets. The Account Executive will primarily lead customer-facing sales motions and will also work with Stripe’s Partnerships team and our BNPL partners on strategic three-party opportunities.

What you’ll do

As an Account Executive, Product focused on Buy Now Pay Later, you will be a quota-carrying product-sales overlay responsible for growing adoption and payment volume across new and existing Stripe users. You will partner closely with Core Account Executives and Customer Success Managers throughout the sales cycle—from identifying and qualifying opportunities through commercial negotiation, technical validation, implementation, activation, and expansion.

You will develop deep expertise in Klarna, Affirm, the BNPL market, and the needs of users operating across APAC. You will lead business and technical conversations with stakeholders ranging from product and engineering teams to C-level executives, helping users understand how BNPL can support their customer experience and growth objectives. For strategic opportunities, you will coordinate across the user, Stripe, and the BNPL provider to align commercial terms, implementation plans, and launch requirements.

You are an adept salesperson who can build value in complex and competitive situations. You are comfortable navigating technical product discussions, complex customer organizations, and multi-party negotiations. You are equally effective with users and internal stakeholders, and you enjoy turning early customer signals into repeatable go-to-market motions.

Responsibilities

  • Deliver against an individual quota by driving adoption and payment volume for Klarna, Affirm and new potential BNPL partners across new and existing Stripe users in APAC.
  • Partner with Core Account Executives and Customer Success Managers to identify, qualify, develop, and close high-potential BNPL opportunities.
  • Build territory and account strategies that reflect user needs and payment preferences across Australia and other priority APAC markets.
  • Lead discovery with business, product, finance, and technical stakeholders and articulate a clear value proposition for BNPL adoption.
  • Develop customer-specific business cases that connect BNPL to user growth, customer experience, conversion, and global expansion objectives.
  • Navigate complex sales cycles and lead negotiations involving users, Stripe, and BNPL partners, working closely with Partnerships on commercial structure and partner alignment.
  • Coordinate with Solutions Architecture, Product, Engineering, and Post-Sales teams to translate user requirements into viable solutions and help users progress from decision to implementation and activation.
  • Maintain senior relationships with users and develop productive working relationships with Klarna, Affirm and new potential BNPL partners.
  • Monitor adoption and payment volume after launch, identify expansion opportunities, and work with account teams to address barriers to growth.
  • Serve as an internal and customer-facing BNPL expert, creating enablement and repeatable sales plays that improve the effectiveness of Stripe’s broader field organization.
  • Synthesize market intelligence and user feedback for Product, Engineering, Partnerships, and Marketing to help inform product and go-to-market priorities.
